recreation_prompt_markdown:
# Recreation Prompt

Create a single-file browser game titled "Dr. Vesper Null: Portal Noir." Preserve the source loop exactly as a deterministic six-beat interactive episode: the player taps to start, watches a timed scene, receives two mobile-friendly choices, selects either choice to advance, repeats through six scenes, can pause/resume active scenes, and reaches an end screen with replay. Do not add fail states, branching rules, collision, physics, scoring, or new gestures.

Rebuild the presentation as an unhinged noir detective story centered on a portal scientist. The focal actor is Dr. Vesper Null, a trench-coated scientist-detective with a portal monocle, fedora, lab coat, glowing vial, and unstable rift machinery. Use procedural CSS/DOM art: rain, venetian shadows, fog, evidence dossiers, red string, classified stamps, concentric portals, and absurd case text. HUD terms should read as Case File, Rift, Evidence Locked, Paradox Pressure, and Reopen Case. The final result should visibly differ from the old video drama from screenshots while keeping the deterministic choice-gated episode mechanic.
blueprint_markdown:
# Blueprint

## Current Game Truth
- genre: deterministic interactive video / visual-novel episode
- objective: start the episode, watch each timed scene, make a binary choice at each stop, and reach the final episode-complete screen
- input model: tap/click start, tap/click one of two choices, tap/click pause/resume, tap/click replay
- core loop: scene plays or animates -> choice gate appears -> either choice advances deterministically -> progress dot updates -> next scene begins
- fail/friction state: no fail state; friction is pacing/tension from pauses, choices, and episode completion

## Protected Mechanics
- Six sequential scenes/case beats.
- Two choices per choice gate with equivalent deterministic advancement.
- Progress dots, scene/case label, pause/resume, replay, and end-screen completion.
- No collision, physics, branching scoring, win/loss, or fail-state invention.

## Safe Theming Surfaces
HUD language, scene art, entity silhouettes, background, choice copy, progress labels, feedback badges, fonts, palette, GIF captions, and audio cues are safe to transform because they do not change the deterministic choice-gated loop.
